clue.text: Courteous note returned with the story

indicators.note: returned tells us the note is turned round and read backwards

parts.note: FA is the fourth note of the sol-fa scale
a fable is a moral tale or story

explanation.surface: A polite message sent back along with the tale it accompanied.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' applies only to the note, not to the story that follows.
explanation.definitionFit: An affable person is friendly and polite, a close synonym of courteous.

clue.text: Try to do the work of the devil after returning thanks

indicators.note: after places the devil's work behind the reversed thanks
returning says the word for thanks is read backwards here

parts.note: TA is British informal for thank you

parts.words: do the work of the devil
parts.note: to tempt is to lure into sin, the devil's business

explanation.surface: Someone, having said thanks, then sets about the devil's work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' turns the thanks round, and 'after' puts the devil's work behind it. TA is British slang for thank you.
explanation.definitionFit: To attempt something is to have a go at it, the same as a try.

clue.text: Citizen's right of males in foreign country

indicators.note: in places the males' word inside the country's name

parts.note: France is a country abroad from a British viewpoint
HIS marks things for men, as on a door reading 'his' and 'hers'

explanation.surface: A remark on the civil rights of men in another land.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' signals the container; 'males' is read as the label on a men's door, 'his' as opposed to 'hers'.
explanation.definitionFit: The franchise is the right to vote, held by a citizen.

clue.text: Man swallowed by animal as a drink

indicators.note: swallowed by puts the man inside the animal, as a snake engulfs its prey

parts.note: a boa is a large constricting snake
HE is the pronoun for a man

explanation.surface: A man engulfed by a snake, as if the snake were having a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Bohea is a kind of black China tea, so a drink.

clue.text: Make it possible for an egghead to apprehend the French

parts.note: the head, or first letter, of egg is E
to nab is to arrest or apprehend
LE is French for the

explanation.surface: Allowing a clever intellectual to arrest some French people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'egghead' is read as the head of 'egg', its first letter E, not as an intellectual.
explanation.definitionFit: To enable is to allow or give the means to do something.

clue.text: Less healthy so trouble starts for the painter

parts.note: sicker means more ill, so less healthy

indicators.note: starts picks out the opening letter of trouble

explanation.surface: An ill person whose trouble is just beginning.
explanation.walkthrough: Walter Sickert was an English painter of the Camden Town Group.
explanation.definitionFit: Walter Sickert was a British impressionist artist, so a painter.

clue.text: Sketch which shows different races in love

indicators.note: different says the letters are made into a different arrangement

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, shaped like O

explanation.surface: An outline showing various ethnic groups falling in love.
explanation.walkthrough: 'different' rearranges RACES and IN to SCENARI; love, nil in tennis, adds O.
explanation.definitionFit: A scenario is an outline or sketch of a plot or situation.

clue.text: Girl has to study deportment

parts.note: to con is to study or learn by heart
stance is bearing or posture, as is deportment

explanation.surface: A young woman obliged to take lessons in posture.
explanation.definitionFit: Constance is a female first name, so a girl.

clue.text: Something hot in the autumn months

definitions.meaning: a glowing piece of coal left in a dying fire
the ... months are the late-year months whose names end in -...: September, November, December

explanation.surface: Something glowing found in late autumn.
explanation.walkthrough: September, November and December all end in the letters of the answer, which is why they are called the ember months.
explanation.definitionFit: An ember is a smouldering fragment of a fire, still hot; the late months share its letters at their end.

clue.text: Return the sweet because it has got hairs on it?

indicators.note: Return asks for the pudding's name to be read backwards

parts.note: sweet is British for dessert, the pudding course

explanation.surface: Sending back a pudding because a hair has been found in it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Return' turns DESSERT round. Sweet is the British word for the pudding course.
explanation.definitionFit: Tressed means having tresses, long locks of hair.

clue.text: A vehicle returns without a man but it enables one to breathe

indicators.note: without here means outside, so the man is placed within
returns tells us the vehicle phrase is read backwards

parts.note: a cart is a simple wheeled vehicle
HE is the pronoun for a man

explanation.surface: A car comes back lacking its driver, yet something lets one breathe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returns' turns the whole phrase A CART round; 'without' is used in its old sense of outside, not lacking.
explanation.definitionFit: The trachea, or windpipe, carries air to the lungs.

clue.text: Honour in time when no blessings ensue

indicators.note: in signals the answer sits inside the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: In time, when no blessings come after.
explanation.definitionFit: To ennoble is to raise to the nobility, so to honour.

clue.text: School periods which enable a boy to become proficient in writing

parts.note: Michael is a boy's name
to master a skill is to become proficient in it
MS is the abbreviation for manuscript, a piece of writing

explanation.surface: Terms that let a lad become a skilled writer.
explanation.walkthrough: The autumn term at Oxford, Cambridge and some schools is named after Michaelmas, the feast of St Michael on 29 September.
explanation.definitionFit: Michaelmas terms are autumn terms at schools and universities, so school periods.

clue.text: T-shirt ruined as a result of wanting a drink

indicators.note: ruined suggests the garment's letters are wrecked into a new order

explanation.surface: A spoilt T-shirt, from someone grabbing a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Thirst is the need or craving for drink.

clue.text: An oriental takes the air in the London district

indicators.note: in places the breathing verb inside the district's letters

parts.note: SE is the South East London postal district
to inhale is to breathe air in

explanation.surface: An Asian visitor strolling for fresh air in part of London.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' signals the container. SE stands for south-east London, one of the capital's postal districts.
explanation.definitionFit: A Sinhalese is a member of the majority people of Sri Lanka, an Asian.

clue.text: The animal wasted away if he didn't have a little drink

indicators.note: have, as in hold, says the drink is held within the wasting verb

parts.note: to pine is to waste away through grief or longing
a nip is a small measure of spirits

explanation.surface: A creature that would have pined away without a tot of spirits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'have' signals the container: the wasting verb holds the tot. The surface's 'if he didn't' is padding for the story of a creature pining for drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A pinniped is a fin-footed mammal such as a seal or walrus.

clue.text: She deals in sex and makes love with an animal, in the newspapers

indicators.note: in puts the love and animal pieces inside the newspapers

parts.note: the press means newspapers collectively
love is zero in tennis, shaped like O
a cur is a mongrel dog

explanation.surface: A tabloid story about a woman in the sex trade and her bestial affair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' signals the container; 'makes' and 'with' only join the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A procuress is a woman who obtains prostitutes for clients.

clue.text: The unfamiliar tune died, having not been prepared for publication

indicators.note: unfamiliar says the letters are put into a strange new order

explanation.surface: An obscure tune faded away before it could be published.
explanation.definitionFit: Unedited text has not been revised for printing.

clue.text: Caught resting when doing the chores

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
leaning on something is resting against it

explanation.surface: Someone found leaning idly when supposed to do housework.
explanation.definitionFit: Cleaning is the typical household task, a chore.

clue.text: Around this place the fish stuck together

indicators.note: Around says the fish is wrapped about the place word

parts.note: cod is a common food fish
here means this place

explanation.surface: Fish clustering around this spot.
explanation.definitionFit: To cohere is to stick together, so cohered means clung together.

clue.text: Hat for Iron Lady

parts.note: Fe is the chemical symbol for iron
Dora is a woman's name

explanation.surface: A hat for Margaret Thatcher, the Iron Lady.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Iron Lady' suggests Margaret Thatcher, but here the two words work separately.
explanation.definitionFit: A fedora is a soft felt hat with a creased crown.

clue.text: Not senile but one's sea legs are unsteady

indicators.note: unsteady says the letters of the phrase wobble into a new order

explanation.surface: Not doddery, yet unsteady on board.
explanation.definitionFit: Ageless means not ageing, so free of senility.

clue.text: Something lucky found in old woman's bed

parts.note: ma is mother, the old woman, so ma's
a cot is a small bed

explanation.surface: A charm discovered in an elderly woman's bed.
explanation.definitionFit: A mascot is a person or object thought to bring good luck.

clue.text: The tough and speedy are on top-there's no getting away from it

definitions.text: there's no getting away from it

parts.note: hard means tough
fast means speedy
to rule is to be on top, in charge

explanation.surface: The strong and swift dominate, an inescapable fact of life.
explanation.definitionFit: A hard and fast rule is fixed and admits no exceptions.

clue.text: The florid features of an author's prose style

indicators.note: of an author's points to the answer lying within the writer's own words that follow

explanation.surface: Commenting on the flowery qualities of a writer's style.
explanation.definitionFit: Roses in the cheeks are a rosy, ruddy complexion, the marks of a florid face.

clue.text: Channel of communication in which a sailor holds a degree

indicators.note: holds says the sailor contains the degree

parts.note: tar is an old word for a sailor
MA is a Master of Arts degree

explanation.surface: A conduit through which a seaman carries a qualification.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tamar is a river forming most of the border between Devon and Cornwall in England.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tamar is a river, a natural channel linking places.

clue.text: Esteem a measure reduced during the interval

indicators.note: during places the shortened measure within the interval

parts.note: a rest is an interval or pause

indicators.note: reduced means the measure loses its last letter

parts.note: a peck is a dry measure of a quarter bushel

explanation.surface: Admiration for a modest amount during the break.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reduced' drops the last letter of the measure; 'during' places what is left within the interval.
explanation.definitionFit: Respect is regard or admiration, as is esteem.

clue.text: Turn up carrying the favourite to take part in the race

indicators.note: carrying says the arrival word holds the favourite inside

parts.note: to come is to arrive, or turn up
a pet is a favourite

explanation.surface: Turning up at the race with the favourite in tow.
explanation.definitionFit: To compete is to take part in a contest.

clue.text: Stretch the limit of the area

indicators.note: of reads as belonging to, so the limit comes at the close of the area

parts.note: dist. is the abbreviation for district, an area
an end is a limit or boundary

explanation.surface: Push the boundary of the region.
explanation.definitionFit: To distend is to swell or stretch outward.

clue.text: Attacks although the shortened article shows signs of deterioration

indicators.note: shortened means the article loses its final letter

parts.note: the is the definite article
metal that rusts shows corrosion

explanation.surface: Assaults, though the abridged piece is showing wear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shortened' drops the final letter of the article; 'shows signs of deterioration' is one verb phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Thrusts are forceful lunges, attacks with a weapon.
